claim: A split git index and `index.skipHash` cannot both be on. This repository sets `index.skipHash`, which writes the index checksum as zeros, and a split index names its shared file by that checksum, so the file is written as `sharedindex.0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` and the link recorded in the index is zeros too. Git reads a zero link as no shared index, so every entry disappears: 352,450 to none, twice on this checkout and twice in a worktree. With `index.skipHash=false` the shared file takes a real name and every entry is kept. No commit was ever harmed, because a landing builds its tree from the tree at HEAD rather than from the index. Once both are measured honestly the split index is worth about 9ms of a 178ms hold, which is not worth having.

evidence:
Measured on 2026-09-16 with git 2.55.0, against this repository, whose index holds about 352,450 entries in 58MiB. `git config --local --get index.skipHash` answers true here, and nothing sets it globally.

In one linked worktree, with the index whole at 352,450 entries: `git update-index --split-index` left `git ls-files` answering nothing, the index at 3.1MiB, and one shared file named `sharedindex.0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`. The index was put back, and `git -c index.skipHash=false update-index --split-index` over the same index kept all 352,450 entries and wrote a second shared file named `sharedindex.ca84a35c...`. The name is the difference: a shared index is named by the index checksum, `index.skipHash` writes that checksum as zeros, and git reads a zero link as no shared index at all.

The same emptying happened twice on this checkout, once from `git config core.splitIndex true` letting the next write convert, and once from `--split-index` run directly. Each time `folder-matches-a-shape` refused every folder it was handed, which is what a check reading an empty tree says, so every landing in that window was refused. `git read-tree HEAD` put the index back in 343ms with nothing staged, and the commits across both windows were all ordinary.

With every entry kept, one path staged and `git status --porcelain -uno` on the same worktree: whole index with skipHash on, as this repository runs today, 65.3ms and 530.0ms; whole index with skipHash off, 133.9ms and 528.0ms; split index with skipHash off, 55.9ms and 514.5ms. So skipHash halves a whole-index write on its own, a split index beats it by about 9ms, and `git status` is untouched by either.

Every earlier number said to be larger than that was taken after the emptying, against an index holding nothing, including `stage 63ms to 14ms`, `status 477ms to 9ms`, and three hundred stages at mean 14.4ms. A `--shared` clone, which inherits no local config and so ran with skipHash off, took akasha's own `committed` from 150.0ms and 146.4ms to 76.1ms, 71.8ms and 72.0ms: that is the 134ms case against the 56ms case rather than a halving of what this repository does.

Index version 4 was measured on a whole index: the file went from 58MiB to 34MiB and a write from 63ms to 65ms, so shrinking the file buys nothing.
